slides.title: Plan your ideas.
slides.notes: Ask: what do you think this lesson is about? Today we plan the essay from both sides of the topic card.

slides.title: Why is this lesson important?
slides.body:
• Good writers plan before they write.
  • Both sides make your opinion stronger.
  • A clear plan makes writing faster.
slides.notes: Frame: a plan is the map for the essay.

slides.title: Pair Talk
slides.body:
What did you learn in lesson 1?

Which side did you choose?

Tell your partner.

Opinion — Reason — Evidence
slides.notes: Recap lesson 1: the task needs both sides, then your opinion. Students restate their position.

slides.title: Strategy: Organize for and against
slides.body:
DoPut the advantages in one paragraph.
WhyThe reader sees each side clearly.
HowDo the same for the disadvantages.
slides.notes: Page 133, Writing strategy. One paragraph for each side.

slides.title: Strategy: Generate ideas
slides.body:
DoThink of many points for each side.
WhyMore ideas mean stronger choices.
HowThink of people you know. What would they say?
slides.notes: Page 133, Writing strategy. Online research can add more ideas.

slides.title: Page 133, Exercise 2
slides.body:
Match each note to a topic.

Say if it is for or against.
slides.notes: Notes a-d on page 133. Students match in pairs, then check the answers.

slides.body:
Page 133, Exercise 2

TaskMatch the notes to the topics.
asaves the cutting down of trees = reading books on digital devices (for)
bencourages social interaction = social media (for)
clack of feedback from a teacher = studying online (against)
dmeet and play with new people = online gaming (for)
slides.notes: Reveal row by row. Check: a, b and d are advantages; c is a disadvantage.

slides.title: Strategy: Cut your notes
slides.body:
DoCut words from your notes.
WhyShort notes are easy to use.
HowKeep only the key information.
slides.notes: Page 133, Writing tip. Short notes become a good habit.

slides.title: Try it: Cut the notes
slides.body:
Try it: Cut the notes
Original: it helps you practice speaking English at home
Which note keeps the key idea?
 practices speaking English at home
 helps practice English
 it helps you practice speaking English at home
slides.notes: Ask: which note is short and keeps the key idea? Then click.

slides.title: Try it: Cut the notes
slides.body:
Try it: Cut the notes
Original: it helps you practice speaking English at home
Which note keeps the key idea?
 practices speaking English at home
✓helps practice English
 it helps you practice speaking English at home
slides.notes: The middle note keeps the key idea in three words. Short notes save time.

slides.body:
Page 133, Exercise 3

TaskReduce the notes.
1saves cutting down trees → saves trees
2encourages social interaction
3no feedback from teacher
4meet/play new people
slides.notes: Reveal row by row. Notes keep only the key words.

slides.title: Page 134, Exercise 4
slides.body:
Write your arguments in the For or Against columns.

Add what another person might say.
slides.notes: Five minutes. Timer starts automatically. Monitor: ideas in both columns.

slides.title: Strategy: Select and order
slides.body:
DoChoose the strongest ideas.
WhyYou have space for only two or three.
HowDecide the order. Join ideas in one sentence.
slides.notes: Page 134, Writing strategy. Start or finish with the strongest point.

slides.body:
Page 134, Exercise 6 (1)

QuestionWhich arguments are joined in one sentence?
AnswerParagraph 2: "Second, you can create your own playlists, and what's more, share them with friends easily." Paragraph 3: "There's also the fact that some artists don't appear on streaming services, and another argument against them is that they don't pay artists much."
ExplanationLinking phrases join two ideas in one sentence.
Transcript"what's more" and "another argument against them is"
slides.notes: Page 132 model. These linking phrases will become key phrases in lesson 3.

slides.body:
Page 134, Exercise 6 (2)

QuestionWhich paragraph begins with the strongest argument?
AnswerParagraph 2.
ExplanationIt starts with "First, and most importantly, ..."
Transcript"First, and most importantly, streaming means you can listen to your favorite songs anywhere, on any device, without using up memory on it."
slides.notes: The writer puts the strongest advantage first.

slides.body:
Page 134, Exercise 6 (3)

QuestionWhich paragraph has one of the strongest points at the end?
AnswerParagraph 3.
ExplanationIt ends with the strongest disadvantage.
Transcript"Last but not least, when you stream music, unfortunately you don't own it at all."
slides.notes: The writer finishes the paragraph with its strongest point.

slides.title: Page 134, Exercises 5 and 6
slides.body:
Read one column to your partner.

Partner: make the opposite argument.

Select and order your notes.
slides.notes: Six minutes. Timer starts automatically. Exercise 5 pair work, then Exercise 6 question 4: select and order notes. Collect the plans.

slides.title: Your plan is ready
slides.body:
You know your topic. You planned both sides.

Next lesson: we write the essay.
slides.notes: Collect the plans. Preview lesson 3: drafting the essay.
